summary: Full review: the round-4 blocker (inline --question JSON in shell) is removed by --question-file <path>|- and every protocol.md/SKILL.md call site now uses it; no new blocking defect, but the inline '<answer>'/'<recommended>' argument remains shell-interpolated and the round-4 relay-record advisories are unchanged.

findings.summary: The answer text is still placed inside shell single quotes with no escaping rule, and this diff makes that the documented form for every relay reply, so an apostrophe in a user reply or an agent-generated recommendation breaks the command or injects shell.
findings.evidence: ENG-25. protocol.md:112 (new in this diff) has 'Write each answer immediately with `factory answer <qid> '<answer>' --question-file <temp-file>`'. On origin/main, step 4 had no shell form, so this extends the pattern to every user reply. protocol.md:110 and SKILL.md:53, :78 and :86 interpolate '<recommended>', which comes from agent output over repository content, the same threat model that SKILL.md:60 cites for question JSON. SKILL.md:146 adds '<answer>' for verdict questions. A reply such as "don't" closes the quote. The '<recommended>' form already existed on origin/main, and SEC1-SCOPE covered only the question JSON, so this is advisory.
findings.fix: Give the answer the same file/stdin form (for example --answer-file <path>|-, or read both answer and question from one JSON file), or add one explicit shell-escape rule in protocol.md Relay (each ' becomes '\''). Add a test with an apostrophe in the answer.

findings.summary: An identical-answer retry commits any edits to a relay record that is already tracked, as long as its Answer JSON line is unchanged.
findings.evidence: ENG-26 / FR-008 (records are immutable). Lines 1596-1625 compare only lines[4]. When the record is tracked but dirty, they call commit_worktree('factory: answer <qid>'), so changed Origin, question or option lines are committed. The code has not changed since round 4.
findings.fix: When the record is tracked at HEAD and its working copy differs, refuse with exit 1. Finish a pending commit only for an untracked record that matches render_relay_record output.

findings.summary: The retry commit path calls commit_worktree without taking the run lock.
findings.evidence: ENG-23 / ENG-26. Lines 1607-1625 run git ls-tree, git status and commit_worktree with no write_run or lock acquisition. Only the first-answer path goes through write_run. The code has not changed since round 4.
findings.fix: Take the run lock around the clean/dirty check and the commit, and refuse when a live owner holds the lock.

findings.summary: The record existence check runs before write_run and the exclusive create runs after it, so two concurrent answers to one qid can leave the state and the committed record in disagreement.
findings.evidence: ENG-23 / ENG-26. The check at line 1596 and record_path.open('x') at about line 1663 are both outside the lock that write_run takes. The code has not changed since round 4.
findings.fix: Do the record check, the state write and the exclusive record creation under one run lock.

findings.summary: Question validation checks only the type and the id, so a malformed text or options field fails rendering after the state write and leaves an empty record that blocks retries.
findings.evidence: ENG-17 / ENG-26. Line 1572 checks only isinstance(question, dict) and the id. render_relay_record iterates question['options'] and formats the title and text inside record_path.open('x') after write_run (lines 1658-1666). --question-file now feeds the same validation. The code has not changed since round 4.
findings.fix: Validate title and text as strings and options as a list, and render into memory before write_run. Open the file only after rendering succeeds.

findings.summary: A symlinked relay directory in the worktree sends the record outside the worktree, because only the qid and stage name parts are validated.
findings.evidence: ENG-25. record_path.parent.mkdir(...) and open('x') follow symlinks in parent directories. The regex at lines 1586-1590 checks only the file-name parts. The code has not changed since round 4. The exposure is limited because the repository belongs to the user.
findings.fix: Refuse when record_path.parent.resolve() is not under the resolved worktree spec_dir.

findings.summary: The --design-fix value is stored as review.pending_design_fix.verdict with no shape check.
findings.evidence: ENG-25. Lines 1060-1064 store design_fix verbatim. The input comes from the orchestrator, and no harmful use has been shown.
findings.fix: Reject an empty, absolute or '..'-containing value with exit 1 before the state write.
